app.title: GuidML · Guided AutoML
app.tagline: Guided, auditable AutoML for tabular data

auth.headline: Analyse your data without writing code
auth.intro: Upload an Excel or CSV file. GuidML recommends the analysis type, the target and the algorithms, evaluates them on an independent test split, and keeps an auditable history of every version.
auth.feature4: Versioned datasets and one-click audit export
auth.name: Name

projects.title: My projects
projects.emptyText: Upload your first dataset. GuidML profiles it, recommends a task and an algorithm, and keeps the results in a dashboard.
projects.deleteText: Project “{name}” and all of its versions and results will be permanently deleted. Continue?

upload.title: New project: upload your dataset
upload.subtitle: Each project is an independent dataset with its own dashboard and version history.
upload.dropText: Drop the file here or click to browse
upload.formats: Excel (.xlsx) or CSV, up to 50 MB
upload.created: Project created — now choose the analysis type

wizard.reconfigureNotice: You are changing the analysis settings. After choosing a model, all {count} data versions are re-analysed with the new settings so that they stay comparable.

problem.title: Initial dataset profile
problem.intro: Your dataset has {rows} rows and {columns} columns. Each task below is labelled by deterministic rules; the final choice is yours.
problem.rulesNote: Statuses come from documented rules (row count, usable features, target candidates) — they are not probabilities.

target.title: Choose the outcome to predict (Target)
target.detectedIntro: These columns look like observed outcomes. The highlighted one is the system suggestion; the choice is yours.
target.noneFound: No obvious outcome column was found. Choose one of the options below to run classification.
target.manualText: Choose a user-selected target from the columns that are suitable as labels.
target.clusteringText: Group similar rows without any target.
target.aiText: An LLM suggests 2–4 numeric columns; a deterministic, reproducible rule turns them into Low / Medium / High classes. The result is synthetic — it is not a real-world outcome.
target.privacyText: only aggregated column summaries (names, types, missing ratios, quartiles, distinct counts) are sent to the external LLM provider (OpenRouter). No row values or category labels are shared.
target.abortOnFailure: Stop with an error if the LLM fails (instead of a labelled statistical fallback)
target.noManual: No column here is suitable as a manual target (columns are identifiers or have too many distinct numeric values).

classification.title: Predict a defined outcome (Classification)
classification.description: The system learns patterns from labelled rows and predicts the class of new rows.
examples: Assigning a category to a new record

clustering.title: Find groups of similar rows (Clustering)
clustering.description: Without any predefined answer, the system groups rows that share similar feature values.

evidence.NO_TARGET_AND_NO_NUMERIC: No target candidate and no numeric column for a pseudo-target
evidence.PSEUDO_TARGET_REQUIRED: No label column — a pseudo-target would be required
evidence.NO_STRONG_TARGET: No observed target column — grouping is natural
evidence.TARGET_EXISTS_CLASSIFICATION_LIKELY: A target column ({column}) exists — classification may fit better
evidence.TARGET_KEYWORD: Column name suggests an outcome or status

codes.TOO_FEW_ROWS: Only {rows} rows; at least {min_rows} are needed.
codes.SMALL_DATASET: Small dataset ({rows} rows): results may be unstable; {recommended}+ rows are recommended.
codes.INFINITE_VALUES: Infinite values in {columns} were treated as missing.
codes.MIXED_TYPES_COERCED: Mostly numeric text columns were converted to numbers: {columns}.
codes.MIXED_TYPES: Columns with mixed value types are treated as categories: {columns}.
codes.HIGH_CARDINALITY: High-cardinality columns keep their {max_categories} most frequent categories: {columns}.
codes.TARGET_MISSING_ROWS: {count} rows without a target value are excluded.
codes.TARGET_TOO_FEW_CLASSES: The target has fewer than two classes.
codes.IMBALANCED_TARGET: Severely imbalanced classes (largest/smallest = {ratio}); prefer Macro-F1 and balanced accuracy.
codes.SCHEMA_TYPE_CHANGED: Column types differ from the first version: {columns}.

pseudo.circularityWarning: This target is synthetic. A classifier that also sees the generator features can simply reconstruct the rule, so its score measures rule reconstruction, not real-world prediction. The dashboard reports both conditions (with / without generator features).
pseudo.generatorFeatures: Generator features (↑ higher = higher level, ↓ reversed)
pseudo.fitScope: fitted on the version-1 training split only
pseudo.labelPolicy: frozen for later versions (new rows use the same cut-offs)
pseudo.missingPolicy: missing values filled with the training median

reason.STATISTICAL_PCA: The columns {features} share the largest common variation (first principal axis). Each row is scored by the average rank of these columns and placed in Low / Medium / High using training-split cut-offs.

notices.LLM_FALLBACK_STATISTICAL: The LLM was not used ({reason}). The pseudo-target was built with the statistical generator and is labelled as such everywhere.

prefs.title: Analysis preferences
prefs.intro: answer two questions to rank compatible algorithms.
prefs.growthQuestion: Will new data be added over time?
prefs.growthNo: No, the data is mostly static

clusterPrefs.title: Clustering preferences
clusterPrefs.fallbackNotice: Instead of predicting, the system will group similar rows.
clusterPrefs.goalQuestion: What is the goal of grouping?
clusterPrefs.goalSegmentation: Understand segments and how they relate (hierarchy)
clusterPrefs.goalPatterns: Discover hidden patterns (clusters may be irregular)
clusterPrefs.countQuestion: Do you know the number of clusters?
clusterPrefs.countUnknown: No — let the system choose it
clusterPrefs.countInvalid: The number of clusters must be an integer of at least 2

autoDetect.title: Detected automatically from the data
autoDetect.intro: You do not need to answer these: they were measured on the dataset and are used as evidence for the compatibility score.
autoDetect.noiseText: {outliers} of rows contain outliers and {missing} of cells are empty.
autoDetect.dimensionText: {features} input columns ({encoded} features after encoding) for {rows} rows.
autoDetect.dimensionEffect: Algorithms suited to high-dimensional data gain evidence points.

models.title: Algorithm compatibility ranking
models.intro: Ineligible algorithms are filtered out first; the remaining ones are ranked by a bounded Compatibility Score (0–100) built from your answers and the detected data traits.
models.semantics: The Compatibility Score describes how well an algorithm's documented strengths match your data and goals. It is a transparent heuristic prior — it does not predict accuracy or F1.
models.noStrengths: No strength matched the collected evidence.
models.formulaText: Each evidence item e (your goals: +40 if it is a strength, −15 if a weakness; detected data traits: ±10) is summed into raw(a). R is the maximum attainable sum, so the score always lies in [0, 100]; 50 means no evidence either way.
models.failed: Model recommendation failed. Use “Previous step” to review the settings and try again.
models.none: No eligible algorithm for these settings. Use “Previous step” to change your answers.
models.done: Analysis complete and saved to the project

eligibility.SVM_TOO_MANY_ROWS: kernel SVM is limited to 20,000 rows (quadratic cost)
eligibility.KNN_TOO_MANY_ROWS: KNN is limited to 50,000 rows (slow prediction)
eligibility.DBSCAN_CANNOT_FIX_CLUSTER_COUNT: DBSCAN cannot use a fixed number of clusters
eligibility.AGGLOMERATIVE_TOO_MANY_ROWS: agglomerative clustering is limited to 10,000 rows (quadratic memory)

capability.known_clusters: Suits a known number of clusters
capability.unknown_clusters: Finds the number of clusters itself

loading.aiTarget: Building the pseudo-target (the LLM may take a moment)…
loading.training: Training on the training split and evaluating on the test split…
loading.addingVersion: Adding the new rows and analysing the new version…

help.accuracy: Share of test rows predicted correctly.
help.balanced_accuracy: Mean recall over classes; robust to class imbalance.
help.macro_f1: Unweighted mean of per-class F1; every class counts equally.
help.weighted_f1: Per-class F1 weighted by class frequency.
help.precision: Of the rows predicted as a class, how many truly belong to it.
help.recall: Of the rows of a class, how many the model found.
help.silhouette: Cohesion vs. separation of clusters, from −1 to 1 (higher is better).
help.davies_bouldin: Average similarity of each cluster to its closest neighbour (lower is better).
help.calinski_harabasz: Ratio of between- to within-cluster dispersion (higher is better).
help.noise_ratio: Share of rows labelled as noise (DBSCAN).
help.stability: Mean ARI between the full solution and refits on 80% subsamples.

clusterWarning.SINGLE_CLUSTER: Fewer than two clusters were found; internal indices are undefined.
clusterWarning.MICRO_CLUSTERS: Some clusters are very small (<1% of rows).
clusterWarning.SMALL_DATASET: Small dataset: cluster structure may be unstable.

selectionCriterion.silhouette: number of clusters chosen by silhouette (internal)
selectionCriterion.dbscan: eps / min_samples chosen by silhouette × (1 − noise ratio)

rowDrop.TEST_CLASS_UNSEEN_IN_TRAIN: {count} test rows of a class absent from training

dashboard.addData: + Add new rows to this dataset
dashboard.nextContinueText: Append new rows with the same columns to create a new cumulative version and compare it with earlier ones.
dashboard.nextNewText: Create an independent project with its own dashboard.

protocol.title: Evaluation protocol
protocol.preprocessingValue: fitted on training rows only; applied to test rows

classification.title: Classification results — {algorithm}
classification.pseudoWarning: Synthetic pseudo-target: the headline scores measure how well the labelling rule is reconstructed. See the circularity ablation below for the independent-signal condition.
classification.testNote: All scores are measured on {rows} independent test rows that were never used for fitting.
classification.fixedHoldout: Fixed version-1 hold-out ({rows} rows): Macro-F1 {f1}, accuracy {acc}. Use this to compare versions on identical test rows.
classification.confusionHint: Rows: actual class · columns: predicted class.

importance.title: Feature importance (permutation, test split)
importance.method: Method: permutation importance on the independent test split — drop in Macro-F1 when a column is shuffled (5 repeats). Comparable across model families.
importance.disclaimer: Importance reflects predictive association within this model, not causation.
importance.none: Feature importance is not available for this run.

clustering.title: Clustering results — {algorithm}
clustering.interpretation: Internal indices are computed on non-noise points and describe geometric cohesion and separation in feature space — not the business meaning of the clusters.
clustering.userK: number of clusters set by the user
clustering.scatterHint: Rows projected on the first two principal components of the preprocessed features.
clustering.profilesHint: For each cluster, the three columns whose mean differs most from the overall mean (in standard deviations).
clustering.noProfiles: No numeric columns available for profiles.

ablation.title: Circularity ablation (pseudo-target)
ablation.intro: Condition A keeps the generator features in the model input; condition B removes them. A large gap means the model mainly reconstructs the rule.
ablation.drift: Label drift if the rule were re-fitted
ablation.note: Low scores in condition B do not mean the model failed: they show how much independent signal the remaining columns carry.

versions.title: Data versions (cumulative)
versions.hint: Version n = all rows of versions 1…n; every version is retrained from scratch. Rows keep their train/test membership across versions.
versions.notAnalysedYet: This version has not been analysed yet
versions.deleteText: Version {n} and the rows it added will be deleted. Earlier versions are not affected.
versions.comparisonNote: Changes across versions can come from distribution shift, class balance or an easier test set. The v1 hold-out column compares versions on identical test rows.
versions.comparisonNoteClustering: Internal indices are recomputed on each cumulative dataset; differences reflect the data as well as the model.

update.title: Add new rows to this dataset
update.text: New rows are appended to the previous data and the analysis is repeated on the whole cumulative dataset with the same settings. The result is stored as a new version.
update.columns: The new file must contain exactly these columns (order does not matter):
update.dropText: Drop the file with new rows here or click
update.chooseFirst: Choose the file with new rows first
